claims.text: Nudges influence behavior by altering the decision-making environment without restricting options or altering financial incentives.
Multiple types of nudges succeed in altering behavior across diverse domains.
Nudges that automate aspects of the decision-making process produce an average effect size (Cohen's d) that is 0.193 larger than other nudges.

evidence.description: Researchers across behavioral sciences disciplines, utilizing varied data sources, have documented successful behavioral change across a wide range of domains.
Analysis of 174 articles estimating nudge treatment effects showed that nudges automating decision-making had an average Cohen's d 0.193 larger than other nudges.

methodologies.name: Meta-analytic review of nudge treatment effects
methodologies.description: Analyzed 174 empirical articles estimating nudge treatment effects alongside qualitative analysis of successful and unsuccessful nudges.

future_work.text: Determining which types of nudges tend to be most impactful.
Using field and laboratory research approaches as complementary methods.
Considering effects of nudges on non-targeted outcomes.
Examining interaction effects among nudges and other interventions.
